extracted.intended_audience: public relations professionals and communicators (Germany); members and stakeholders of the German Council for Public Relations (DRPR)
extracted.subtask_description: Organization-level guidance and enforcement practices from the German Council for Public Relations (DRPR) concerning ethical behaviour, applicable codes, and complaint/disciplinary procedures in PR and public communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical behaviour in the profession
rubrics_metrics.description: On the basis of industry codes, the DRPR develops and updates guidelines for ethical behaviour in the profession and deals with cases in which the rules are violated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Council's mission is voluntary self-regulation: it formulates and updates ethical guidelines, monitors adherence, and handles violations. This is the overarching standard against which conduct is judged; specific codes and guidelines implement it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publicising grievances and issuing sanctions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Council publicises grievances and misconduct and issues warnings or reprimands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When rules are violated the DRPR may make grievances public and impose non-legal sanctions such as warnings or reprimands — indicating that transparency and reputational consequences are part of enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on deliberate deception / misleading content
rubrics_metrics.description: Communications must not deliberately deceive the public; deliberate deception is grounds for reprimand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example cases cited include reprimands for 'fundamental breaches of basic ethical standards of communication' and for 'deliberately deceiving the public' — implying a clear standard against intentional misinformation or deceptive practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and labelling of AI-generated content
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of artificial intelligence that produces content must not be misleading and should be labelled appropriately; unlabelled/misleading AI content can be reprimanded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site cites a reprimand for an association for 'misleading and unlabelled use of artificial intelligence' in social communications, which indicates a specific expectation that AI-generated material be disclosed/labelled to avoid deceiving audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow established codes and complaint procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Complainants and practitioners must use the DRPR's established codes and formal complaint procedures (Anleitung zur Beschwerde, Beschwerdeformular, Beschwerdeordnung) when addressing alleged misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The navigation/menu references multiple formal instruments — communication codes, DRPR guidelines, PR codes, public communication codes, complaint instructions, complaint form, and complaint rules — indicating that adherence to these procedural and normative documents is required for both evaluating conduct and initiating cases.
